output.headline: Provider specialist with an open platform in the target's sub-sector; the add-on route fits a $200M Midwest asset.
output.differentiator: Has an open platform in the target's own sub-sector for an add-on route, with 22 of 24 deals in provider services, backed by a EUR 9 billion fund. [A:angles, P:2]
output.why_them: Add-on to its open platform; provider-focused sponsor with a large fund

acquirer_overview.title: Provider-focused sponsor, active since 2016, with a EUR 9 billion fund
points: Financial sponsor; healthcare is one of four core industries, and 22 of 24 deals are in provider services. [P:1, A:angles]
24 deals from 2016 to 2024; 21 of 24 (88%) closed, 22 of 24 (92%) were control deals, and 9 came since 2022. [T:record, K:closed_share, K:control_share, K:recent]
Fund XI closed at its EUR 9 billion hard cap (about $11 billion), ample capacity for a $200M EV. [P:2]

strategic_fit_thesis.title: Natural add-on to an open platform in the target's sub-sector
points: The open platform in the sub-sector gives an add-on route; Platform Build was the motive in 7 of 24 deals. [A:angles, M:platform_build]
4 deals in the target's own sub-sector and 18 in adjacent provider sub-sectors; sub-sector overlap and deal count are both modest factors in its favour. [T:record, S:sector_rel, S:activity]
Second on the priority list at a 4.8% likelihood; a deal not smaller than its usual range is a slight factor in its favour. [R:rank, S:not_smaller]

precedent_activity.title: Own-sub-sector buyouts show appetite for size and multiples up to 15.0x
points: 2022 Green Medical Center: $1,304M leveraged buyout at 15.0x. 2023 Harbor Medical Center: $991M leveraged buyout at 11.1x. [D:MA-2022-0045, D:MA-2023-0466]
2024 Harbor Health Network: $35M carve-out at 11.6x. 2024 Principal Physician Group: $76M recapitalization in the Midwest at 15.9x. [D:MA-2024-0339, D:MA-2024-0431]
Median deal is $77M; 8 of 24 deals fall in the comparable $100M-$400M size band. [T:record, K:size_band]

valuation_context.title: Upper-quartile pricing is defensible, but the ask sits just short of its return target
points: 70 comparable deals: EV/EBITDA of 10.7x at the 25th percentile, 12.8x median, 15.3x at the 75th. [V:comps]
Target margin of 16.8% beats the comps' 12.9% median and sits above 87% of comps, supporting the 75th percentile; this buyer's median paid is 12.5x. [V:comps, X:target]
At 5.0x leverage the IRR at the ask is 18.7% against a 20% target; maximum price is $193M on a same-multiple exit, $216M at a 15.0x platform exit. [V:lbo]

risk_flags.title: Size stretch
risk_flags.concern: The $200M EV is well above this buyer's typical deal size.
risk_flags.mitigant: It has closed far larger deals, and 8 of 24 sit in the comparable size band.
risk_flags.reality: Median deal is $77M, against a biggest of $1,304M; the size signal is only slightly favourable. [T:record, K:size_band, S:not_smaller]

risk_flags.title: Return at the asking price
risk_flags.concern: The IRR at the ask falls short of the sponsor's return target.
risk_flags.mitigant: A platform exit at 15.0x lifts the maximum price above the $200M ask.
risk_flags.reality: The IRR is 18.7% against 20%; the maximum price is $193M on a same-multiple exit and $216M on a platform exit. [V:lbo]

risk_flags.title: Thin Midwest record
risk_flags.concern: Little history in the target's region.
risk_flags.mitigant: It completed a Midwest recapitalization in 2024 and has bought in neighbouring Great Plains.
risk_flags.reality: Only 2 deals in the target region; region fit is a slight factor against. [T:record, S:geo_fit, D:MA-2024-0431]

conviction.rationale: 4 own-sub-sector and 18 adjacent provider deals, an open platform for an add-on, and second place on the priority list outweigh the one negative: a $77M median deal against the $200M EV. [T:record, A:angles, R:rank, C:conviction]
